title: How does the JIT compiler work in .NET?

data.text: **Question:** How does the JIT compiler work in .NET?

The JIT (Just-In-Time) compiler converts IL (Intermediate Language) code into native machine code at runtime. It compiles methods on-demand when they are first called, balancing startup performance with execution speed.

**JIT Compilation Process:**
1. C# code compiles to IL
2. IL stored in assemblies
3. At runtime, JIT compiles IL to native code
4. Native code cached for subsequent calls
5. Method is executed

**JIT Optimizations:**
- Inlining small methods
- Dead code elimination
- Loop optimizations
- Register allocation
- Branch prediction

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: JIT compiles IL to native code at runtime
Methods are compiled on first call
Tiered compilation balances startup and throughput
data.takeaway: JIT compilation allows .NET to be both portable (IL) and performant (native code).
